records.question: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
search_queries: How many credits do I need to take to be full-time as a graduate student?
records.answer:
As an F-1 or J-1 graduate student, you need to be registered for **at least 9 credits each term** to be full-time. (Undergraduates need 12+.)

Key conditions:
- **Online courses:** Only 3 credits of online/distance coursework can count toward the full-time minimum. At least 6 of your 9 credits must be face-to-face or hybrid.
- **Audited courses** don't count toward the minimum.
- **Less than full time:** If you can't enroll full-time, you must get written permission from ISSS *before* the term begins (or follow the LTFT process and deadlines). Dropping below full-time without authorization can put you out of status.
- **Dropping or withdrawing from a course:** Get approval from an ISSS advisor first.

For your specific situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

Sources:

records.question: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?
search_queries: How many online credits can count toward my full-time enrollment each term?
records.answer:
Only **3 credits** of online or distance coursework can count toward your full-time enrollment each term.

What that means in practice:
- **Undergraduate students** (12+ credits full-time) need at least 9 credits in face-to-face or hybrid courses.
- **Graduate students** (9+ credits full-time) need at least 6 credits in face-to-face or hybrid courses.
- Hybrid classes count as in-person for immigration purposes (per a 2023 ISSS announcement).
- Audited courses don't count toward the full-time minimum.

**Final term:** If you're in your last term and applying for less than full time, you can't take courses fully online. If you need more than one class to finish, no more than one class (3 credits) of online study can count toward your remaining requirements.

Before dropping or withdrawing from any course, or going below full-time, get written approval from an ISSS advisor. Without authorization, you may be considered out of status.

records.question: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
search_queries: How many hours a week can I work on campus while classes are in session?
records.answer:
F-1 and J-1 students can work **no more than 20 hours per week** on campus while school is in session. During an approved vacation term, you may work more than 20 hours per week, but you should check with the Office of Human Resources about their (non-immigration) policies for that period.

Key conditions:
- You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, be a continuing student, have not graduated, and have an unexpired I-20/DS-2019.
- J-1 students must receive prior ISSS authorization for any on-campus employment.
- If you're on co-op, your co-op counts as your "class," so on-campus work is still limited to 20 hours per week. ISSS strongly discourages doing both at the same time.
- On-campus work must not hurt your academic performance. Failing or dropping classes can affect your full-time enrollment and may lead to termination of your SEVIS record.

records.question: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
search_queries: How long is the grace period after I finish my program on an F-1 visa?
records.answer:
F-1 students (and their dependents) have a **60-day grace period** after the program ends, according to the ISSS page on [Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain).

**During the grace period you may:**
- Prepare to leave the U.S.
- Travel within the U.S.

You may **not** work or study. If you aren't applying for OPT or extending your status, you're expected to depart during this time. If you leave before the grace period ends, you can't re-enter in F-1 status after your I-20 expiration date.

**Related points:**
- After Post-Completion OPT ends, you also get a 60-day grace period. This applies only if you completed OPT and didn't exceed the 90-day unemployment limit ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).
- If USCIS receives your OPT application before your 60-day grace period ends, your F-1 status stays active until USCIS decides ([OPT page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)).

**Possible future change:** A DHS proposal from September 2025 would shorten the F-1 grace period from 60 to 30 days ([ISSS announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/September/DHS-Proposes-to-Replace-Duration-of-Status-for-F-and-J-Visa-Holders-with-Fixed-Periods-of-Stay)). It was a proposal, and the excerpts I have don't show it taking effect. Newer ISSS announcements mention a final rule on duration of status (July 2026) that a court postponed (September 2026), so please confirm with an ISSS advisor what applies to your situation.

records.question: How much OPT can I get?
search_queries: How much OPT can I get?
records.answer:
**Standard OPT:** You get a total of 12 months of OPT for each degree level (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate). You can use part of it during your program (pre-completion) or save all 12 months for after graduation (post-completion).
- Pre-completion full-time OPT counts at 100% (6 months used = 6 months deducted).
- Pre-completion part-time OPT counts at 50% (6 months used = 3 months deducted).

**STEM OPT Extension:** If you're in a STEM field and meet the criteria, you may be eligible for an additional 24 months of post-completion OPT. You can't request all 36 months at once. You must first apply for the initial 12 months of post-completion OPT, then apply for the extension while your OPT EAD card is active.

**Recent news:** On October 7, 2026, DHS proposed a rule that would require universities to pay a $70,000 fee for each OPT authorization and $30,000 for subsequent STEM OPT requests. ISSS says this has no immediate impact, and current OPT and STEM OPT processes remain unchanged unless DHS finalizes and implements the rule.

For questions about your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor (isss@drexel.edu).

records.question: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
search_queries: How many days can I be unemployed on post-completion OPT?
records.answer:
You can be unemployed for a maximum of **90 days** in total (an aggregate limit) while on Post-Completion OPT.

Key points:
- Every day counts, including weekends, from the employment start date shown on your EAD until the OPT period ends, if you don't have qualifying employment.
- Qualifying work on Post-Completion OPT must be at least 20 hours per week.
- Going over 90 days is a violation of F-1 status unless you have applied to change educational level or transfer to another SEVP-certified school, departed the U.S., or otherwise acted to maintain legal status. Your SEVIS record may also be terminated.
- Students who exceed the 90-day limit are not eligible for the 60-day grace period.
- If you reach the limit, ISSS advises preparing *before* you hit it.

If you later get a 24-month STEM OPT extension, you get an additional 60 unemployment days, for a maximum of 150 days total. You must report any job loss or interruption to ISSS.

For questions about your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
search_queries: Do I need a job offer to apply for OPT?
records.answer:
No, you don't need a job offer to apply for OPT. The ISSS OPT page says a job offer is not required, but there are conditions once you're on OPT:

- **Post-Completion OPT:** You're expected to actively look for work in your field and be employed for at least nine months after your OPT start date (as shown on your EAD). There is an aggregate limit of 90 days of "unemployment" while on Post-Completion OPT. Each day without qualifying employment counts, including weekends. Before reaching that limit, you should prepare to transfer schools, change educational level, depart the U.S., or otherwise maintain status.
- **Pre-Completion OPT:** There is no penalty for not working, except that the unused time counts against your 12-month OPT eligibility.

You can't start working until you have your EAD and the start date on it has arrived. Working earlier may result in termination of your F-1 status.

**STEM OPT extension:** A job offer is not needed for initial OPT, but the 24-month STEM extension does require a job or job offer directly related to your STEM degree, from an E-Verify employer.

Also, USCIS can take 90 days or longer to process OPT applications. For advice on your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
search_queries: Can I be self-employed during the STEM OPT extension?
records.answer:
No. According to ISSS, self-employment doesn't qualify for the 24-month STEM OPT extension. The regulations require a bona fide employer-employee relationship with an employer, and you can't provide employer attestations on your own behalf.

Some related points from the ISSS page:
- You can work for a start-up, but all regulatory requirements must still be met. That includes an employer with an EIN that is enrolled in and using E-Verify at your worksite, a job directly related to your STEM degree, and a real employer-employee relationship. You can't attest as the employer for yourself.
- Unpaid or volunteer positions also can't be the basis for a STEM OPT extension.
- This differs from standard Post-Completion OPT, where ISSS says you may start a business and be self-employed, as long as you work full-time, hold the proper business licenses, and are actively engaged in a business related to your degree.

If you're planning to run your own company or work at a start-up, I recommend confirming with an ISSS advisor before you apply, since this affects your status.

records.question: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?
search_queries: How recent does the travel signature on my I-20 need to be when I come back to the U.S.?
records.answer:
The answer depends on your situation:

- **F-1 students (regular enrollment):** The Travel Information page says the I-20 needs a travel signature issued within **12 months** of re-entry.
- **F-1 students on Post-Completion OPT or STEM OPT:** The signature must be no older than **6 months**.

The Visa Renewal page says to request a new signature if yours will be more than six months old when you return. A December 2024 advisory also asks for a "recent" travel signature. Since the pages give different timeframes, requesting a signature that is less than six months old before you leave is the safest approach.

If you need a new signature, submit the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs).

Also bring your valid passport, F-1 visa, SEVIS fee receipt, and, if you're on OPT, your EAD card. Proof of employment is optional.

If you're unsure which timeframe applies to you, confirm with an ISSS advisor before traveling.

records.question: How much extra money do I need to show to bring my spouse and one child?

- A copy of the dependent's passport
- An updated official bank statement
- Proof of marriage (for a spouse)

records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?

records.question: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
search_queries: What happens if I'm away from Drexel and not enrolled for more than five months?
records.answer:
If you're not enrolled for more than five months, you can't simply reactivate your SEVIS record. You need to:

- **Apply for and receive a new I-20/DS-2019.**
- **Repay the SEVIS I-901 fee.**
- **Email ISSS at least three months before your planned return** to get instructions on how to apply for the new I-20/DS-2019.

The same applies if your SEVIS record was terminated for a reason other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal."

**Impact on your status:** This kind of absence causes a break in your F-1 status. After you return to the U.S., you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study before you become eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as CPT or OPT.

**Also needed:** To return from a leave of absence, you must first get approval from your academic program. Contact your academic advisor for instructions on reporting your return.

For comparison, if your absence was authorized by ISSS and lasts less than five months, you may be able to request SEVIS reactivation instead. That process is subject to SEVP discretion.

Because this affects your immigration status, I recommend confirming your specific situation with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
search_queries: Can I take less than a full course load in my final term?
records.answer:
Yes, possibly. F-1 and J-1 students in their final term can apply for less than full time (LTFT) under "Completion of Studies" if the credits they still need to finish their program are fewer than full-time enrollment requires (12 for undergraduates, 9 for graduates).

**Conditions:**
- You can't take courses fully online in your final term. If you need more than one class to finish, no more than one class (3 credits) of online study can count toward your remaining requirements.
- Lack of financial support isn't a valid reason to reduce your course load.
- You need ISSS authorization *before* you drop below full time. Dropping without it puts you out of immigration status.

**How to apply:**
1. Complete the Less Than Full-Time form on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx).
2. Your academic advisor must specify the reason and sign it.
3. Email it, with any additional documents in one PDF, to isss@drexel.edu.
4. Wait for ISSS's email approval before changing your registration.

Requests are due by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term).

Also, if you're approved for a *medical* LTFT in your final term, you must still enroll in at least one course.

Because this affects your status, please confirm your specific situation with an ISSS advisor.

Sources: [Less Than Full Time](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/less-than-full-time), [Maintaining F-1 and J-1 Student Status](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/f-1-j-1-maintain)

records.question: How do I apply for CPT?
search_queries: How do I apply for CPT?
records.answer:
To apply for CPT, first confirm that you're eligible, then follow these steps:

**Before you apply**
- You generally need to have been enrolled full-time and physically present in the U.S. for one full academic year (3 quarters or 2 semesters). Some graduate programs that require immediate CPT are an exception.
- You need an internship or training offer directly related to your field.
- The training must be required for all students in your program to graduate, whatever their immigration status. If there's an associated course, you must be registered for it during the CPT term.

records.question: How do I transfer my SEVIS record to another university?

records.answer:
To transfer your SEVIS record out of Drexel, you need to start the process with ISSS before you legally begin studies at the new school.

**Steps**
1. Make sure you are maintaining your F-1 or J-1 status. Only students in valid status can transfer.
2. Complete the [F-1/J-1 SEVIS Transfer Out Form](https://forms.office.com/r/camJYvn38Z?origin=lprLink) and upload the required documents.

**Important**
- Any Drexel employment authorization (on-campus, CPT, OPT, academic training) ends on the transfer date.
- To cancel, change the release date, or switch schools, notify ISSS *before* the release date. After that, ISSS can no longer access your record.

records.question: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
search_queries: How do I apply for a reduced course load for medical reasons?
records.answer:
To apply for a medical reduced course load (LTFT), do the following. Don't drop below full-time until ISSS approves it.

1. **Get a letter from your medical provider.** It must be on official letterhead and signed by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist. It should say that, in their medical opinion, you can't attend classes (or can't attend full-time) during a specific term. ISSS provides a template letter, and the doctor doesn't need to give your diagnosis. If you can't take any courses, the letter must say so clearly.
2. **Complete the Less Than Full-Time form** on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx?source=https%3a%2f%2fdrexel0.sharepoint.com%2fsites%2fISSS-StudentPortal%2fSitePages%2fForms%2fByAuthor.aspx). Your academic advisor must state the reason and sign it.
3. **Email everything as one PDF** (form plus doctor's letter) to isss@drexel.edu.
4. **Wait for ISSS's email decision** before dropping any courses.

**Key conditions:**
- Submit by the add/drop deadline, or at the latest before the withdrawal deadline (Friday of week 7 of the term).
- Approval is required for each term you request.
- Medical LTFT is limited to 12 aggregate months per program level.
- You're expected to return to full-time study afterward.
- In your final term, you must still enroll in at least one course under medical LTFT.

If you drop below full-time without authorization, you're considered out of status. For questions about your own situation, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: What documents do I need to re-enter the U.S. after a trip abroad as an F-1 student?

records.answer:
**Documents for F-1 re-entry** (hand-carry all of them to show Customs and Border Protection):

- Valid passport, valid for more than six months from your return date
- Valid F-1 visa (Canadian and Bermuda citizens are exempt from the visa requirement, per the OPT page)
- Valid Form I-20 with a travel signature issued within 12 months of re-entry
- SEVIS fee payment receipt
- Transcripts or proof of enrollment (optional)

**If you're on Post-Completion OPT or STEM OPT**, you also need:
- A valid EAD card
- Proof of employment, such as an employment letter or paystubs. The STEM OPT page says a letter should state your job title, a brief job description, start and end dates, and salary.
- An I-20 travel signature issued within the past six months, not 12.

**Other tips:**
- To get a travel signature, submit the [Signature Request form](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs).

records.question: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
search_queries: What's the difference between CPT and OPT?
records.answer:
**CPT** and **OPT** are both F-1 off-campus work authorizations, but they differ in purpose and who approves them.

**CPT (Curricular Practical Training)**
- It applies only when an internship, co-op, practicum, or similar training is a **required part of your academic program**. It is driven by the curriculum, not by your wish to work.
- Experience that is merely beneficial or relevant doesn't qualify.
- ISSS reviews and authorizes it.
- Dates follow the official Drexel term dates, and you can't start before the CPT start date. Authorization is term by term, except for Steinbright co-op programs, which follow co-op cycle dates.

**OPT (Optional Practical Training)**
- It is temporary employment directly related to your major and appropriate to your degree level.
- It is available before you finish (Pre-Completion) or after (Post-Completion).
- You apply to USCIS, which can take 90 days or longer.
- A job offer isn't required to apply. During Post-Completion OPT, though, you're expected to actively seek work in your field and be employed for at least nine months after your start date.
- You generally need one full academic year of full-time enrollment, valid F-1 status, and fewer than 365 days of full-time CPT.

**How they connect:** Using 364 days or more of full-time CPT eliminates your OPT eligibility. Part-time CPT and international co-op don't affect it.

Please confirm your own situation with an ISSS advisor.

Sources:
- [CPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/cpt)
- [OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt)

Also, a recent ISSS announcement (Oct 9, 2026) concerns a DHS proposal about OPT fees. You can read it on the ISSS announcements page.

records.question: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
search_queries: Can I work an on-campus job while I'm on co-op?
records.answer:
Yes, but it's strongly discouraged. Here's what ISSS says:

- **Allowed, with a limit:** While you're in your co-op cycle, your co-op job counts as your "class," so on-campus employment is limited to **20 hours per week**.
- **Co-op comes first:** On-campus work must not interfere with your ability to do your co-op job responsibilities.
- **Status requirements:** You must be maintaining valid F-1/J-1 status, and your I-20/DS-2019 must not have expired. You also must not have graduated.
- **J-1 students:** You must get ISSS permission before starting any on-campus job. Email isss@drexel.edu with your job offer, including the position title and expected start and end dates.
- **F-1 students:** You don't need advance ISSS approval, but you do need to complete onboarding and the I-9 with Drexel HR.

If you're unsure how a specific job or co-op arrangement affects your status, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?
search_queries: Tôi có thể làm CPT trong năm học đầu tiên không?

records.question: OPT申请需要多长时间？
search_queries: OPT申请需要多长时间？
records.answer:
**OPT申请的处理时间：** USCIS审理OPT申请可能需要**90天或更长时间**。最新处理时间可查看 [USCIS案件处理时间页面](https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times)（外部链接）。

**需要注意的步骤和时间点：**
- ISSS收到你完整的申请后，大约需要**4-5个工作日**签发OPT I-20。
- 拿到OPT I-20后，需在**30天内**向USCIS提交I-765申请。
- 收到EAD（工作许可卡）之前不能开始工作。

**申请时间窗口：**
- **毕业前OPT（Pre-Completion）：** 最早可在希望开始日期前90天申请。若预计处理时间超过90天，可以考虑更早申请，并选择早于实际入职日期的开始日期。
- **毕业后OPT（Post-Completion）：** 最早可在项目结束日前90天申请，最晚为完成学位要求后60天内。

**加急处理：** 2023年的一则ISSS公告提到，USCIS对部分OPT申请开放了I-907加急处理，费用为$1,500，处理时间为30个日历日。这是2023年的信息，请向ISSS顾问确认目前是否仍适用。

records.question: 졸업 후 F-1 학생의 유예 기간은 얼마나 되나요?
search_queries: 졸업 후 F-1 학생의 유예 기간은 얼마나 되나요?
records.answer:
F-1 학생의 유예 기간(grace period)은 **60일**입니다. J-1 학생은 30일입니다.

**유예 기간 중 가능한 것**
- 출국 준비 및 짐 정리
- 미국 내 여행

**불가능한 것**
- 근무 또는 학업

**OPT/STEM OPT의 경우**
- Post-Completion OPT EAD 카드가 만료된 후 60일의 유예 기간이 있습니다. 이 기간에 새 프로그램 입학(학력 변경 또는 SEVIS 전학), 출국, 또는 다른 방법으로 합법적 신분 유지 조치를 취할 수 있습니다.
- STEM OPT도 EAD 만료 후 60일입니다. 다만 STEM OPT의 경우 EAD 만료일 또는 마지막 실업일 중 빠른 날에 F-1 신분이 종료됩니다.
- OPT를 성공적으로 마친 학생에게만 유예 기간이 주어집니다. OPT 실업 기간 한도(90일, STEM OPT는 150일)를 초과한 경우에는 유예 기간이 없습니다.
- OPT를 신청하지 않거나 체류 신분 연장을 받지 않는 학생은 유예 기간 내에 출국해야 합니다. 유예 기간이 끝나기 전에 출국하면 I-20 만료일 이후 F-1 신분으로 재입국할 수 없습니다.

**향후 변경 가능성**
2025년 9월에 DHS가 제안한 규칙(Duration of Status 폐지)이 시행되면 F-1 유예 기간이 30일로 줄어들 수 있습니다. 2026년 9월 14일 연방 법원이 최종 규칙의 시행일을 연기하는 예비 금지명령을 내렸습니다. 현재 60일이 적용되는 것으로 안내되어 있지만, 본인의 상황은 ISSS 상담 담당자에게 확인하시기 바랍니다.

records.question: Preciso de uma assinatura de viagem no meu I-20 para voltar aos EUA?
search_queries: Preciso de uma assinatura de viagem no meu I-20 para voltar aos EUA?
records.answer:
Sim. Para o F-1, o ISSS lista como documento de viagem um **I-20 válido com assinatura de viagem emitida nos 12 meses anteriores à reentrada**. Se você está em OPT pós-conclusão ou STEM OPT, a assinatura precisa ter sido emitida nos **últimos 6 meses** ([Travel Information](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/travel)).

Na página de renovação de visto, o ISSS diz que você deve solicitar a assinatura se ainda não tiver uma, ou se a sua tiver mais de seis meses no momento em que você quer voltar aos EUA ([Visa Renewal](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/visa-renewal)). Essas duas orientações não coincidem. Por isso, se a sua assinatura tiver entre 6 e 12 meses, confirme com um advisor do ISSS antes de viajar.

**Como solicitar:** use o [formulário de Signature Request](https://drexel.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KHlTvO1gmy8Sfs), indicado em um aviso do ISSS de dezembro de 2024.

**Outros documentos a levar na mão:** passaporte válido por mais de seis meses após a data de retorno, visto F-1 válido, comprovante de pagamento da taxa SEVIS e, opcionalmente, histórico escolar ou comprovante de matrícula.

Como as regras podem mudar, o ISSS recomenda consultá-lo antes de fazer planos de viagem ([aviso de fevereiro de 2025](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/February/Reminder-International-Travel-Immigration-Documents-US-Address-Change)).

records.question: Form I-983
search_queries: Form I-983
records.answer:
**Form I-983** is the STEM OPT training plan. You complete it as part of applying for a STEM OPT extension.

**Getting and filling it out**
- Download it from [DHS Study in the States](https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/stem-opt-hub/additional-resources/form-i-983-overview) (external). ISSS also links the [Form I-983 Instructions [PDF]](https://www.ice.gov/doclib/sevis/pdf/i983Instructions.pdf) (external).
- You don't submit it to USCIS. You submit it to ISSS to get your STEM OPT Request I-20.
- Your employer must complete and sign it. Drexel HR can help Drexel departments with the details, and the employer must be enrolled in E-Verify ([Hiring International Employees](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals)).

**Submitting it to ISSS**
Email isss@drexel.edu the completed I-983 together with the other required items: the STEM OPT Request Form, the processing fee receipt, your OPT EAD card, passport, most recent I-94, and your STEM degree transcript. Send individual PDFs or one compiled PDF, not a zipped folder ([STEM OPT Extension](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)).

**Later requirements while on STEM OPT**
- **Employment changes:** A new employer or changed employer information needs an updated I-983. Report it within 10 days using the [STEM OPT Employment Update Form](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/~/media/Drexel/EMSS-Site-Group/StudentLife/Documents/international-student-support/forms/stem-opt-employment.pdf).
- **Evaluations:** Complete the 1-year self-evaluation and a final evaluation on page 5 of the I-983. Submit them with your [Six-Month Validation Form](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/~/media/Drexel/EMSS-Site-Group/StudentLife/Documents/international-student-support/forms/stem-validation.pdf) within 10 days of the reporting period or end of employment.

If you have questions about your own situation, confirm with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
search_queries: Do I pay the SEVIS I-901 fee again after a long leave?
records.answer:
It depends on how long you're away.

**You must repay the SEVIS I-901 fee** if you were not enrolled for more than five (5) months, or if your SEVIS record was terminated for a reason other than "Authorized Early Withdrawal." In those cases you need a new I-20/DS-2019, and the fee is paid again.

**Steps:**
- Email ISSS at least three (3) months before your planned return to get instructions on applying for the new I-20/DS-2019.
- Pay the fee at [FMJfee.com](https://fmjfee.com/i901fee/index.html), the site ISSS lists for paying the I-901 fee.
- Note that this kind of absence breaks your F-1 status. After you return, you must complete at least one academic year of full-time study before you're eligible for certain F-1 benefits, such as CPT or OPT.

**If your authorized absence is less than five months,** you can request reactivation of your SEVIS record instead. The excerpt doesn't mention a new fee for this. Submit your I-94 travel history, your flight itinerary, and proof of full-time enrollment for the upcoming term at least 1-2 months before returning. SEVP decides at its discretion. If it doesn't approve, you'll need a new I-20, and the five-month rules above apply.

Please confirm your specific situation with an ISSS advisor, since I can't give legal advice.

records.question: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
search_queries: 212(e) two-year home country requirement
records.answer:
**What it is:** The 212(e) requirement applies to some J-1 exchange visitors. Until they have been physically present in their country of nationality or last legal permanent residence for at least two years after leaving the U.S. in J-1 status, they are not eligible for lawful permanent residency or a change to another visa status in the U.S.

**Who it applies to:** According to ISSS, it applies if:
- Your J-1 program was financed in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, by a U.S. government agency or by the government of your country of nationality or last residence, or
- When you were admitted, you were a national or resident of a country that the Department of State designated as needing people with your field of specialized knowledge or skill (the "skills list"). ([New International Students](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/new-international-students) says students receiving government funding or pursuing a major on their home country's skills list are deemed subject to it.)

**Related impact:** If you are subject to 212(e), you cannot begin H-1B employment until you receive a 212(e) waiver ([H-1B FAQ](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/h1b-temp/h1b-faq)).

**Waivers:**
- ISSS may not assist with J-1 waivers, because the Department of State sees this as a conflict of interest. See the [Department of State waiver instructions](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas/study/exchange/waiver-of-the-exchange-visitor.html) (external).
- Once the State Department issues a favorable recommendation, you lose J-1 extension, transfer, and new J-1 visa eligibility.
- Processing can take a year or longer, and applying does not extend your legal stay.

More details are on the [J-1 Exchange Visitors page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/hiring-foreign-nationals/j1-scholars). To find out whether it applies to you, check with an ISSS advisor.

records.question: H-1B cap-gap extension
search_queries: H-1B cap-gap extension
records.answer:
**H-1B cap-gap** is the period between the end of your OPT (or STEM OPT) and the start of your H-1B status. If you're eligible, your work authorization is automatically extended while your change of status is pending.

**Eligibility** ([OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/opt), [STEM OPT](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/stem-opt-extension)):
- Your employer files the H-1B petition on or after April 1 and requests a change of status to begin October 1.
- You're still within your OPT/STEM OPT authorization period when it's filed.

**To get a cap-gap I-20:**
1. Email ISSS to update or confirm your employment and address information. Inaccurate SEVIS information will significantly delay the I-20.
2. Email ISSS one of the following:
   - For cap-gap through June 1: an employer statement that the H-1B change of status was properly filed, plus proof of delivery to USCIS.
   - For cap-gap beyond June 1: a copy of the USCIS receipt, or proof the petition was wait-listed.

ISSS will email you when your new I-20 is ready.

**Good to know:**
- The unemployment limit continues during cap-gap.
- If the petition is denied, rejected, or revoked and your EAD is still valid, work permission ends on the EAD end date. If your OPT already expired, it ends on the rejection, denial, revocation, or withdrawal date.
- Consult your employer or immigration attorney before traveling abroad during cap-gap.

**Length of cap-gap:** The OPT and STEM OPT pages describe an extension through October 1 or approval. A January 2025 [ISSS announcement on the H-1B Modernization Rule](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/January/USCIS-DHS-Announces-H-1B-Modernization-Rule) says the rule extends cap-gap as late as April 1 of the following year. Because the pages differ, please confirm your exact end date with an ISSS advisor.

**Timing for the STEM OPT extension:**

- **Earliest:** You can file up to 90 days before your Post-Completion OPT end date.
- **Send documents to ISSS:** No later than 30 days before your current OPT EAD card end date, so there is time for processing and mailing.

**Note:** ISSS has said USCIS placed a hold on pending applications for people from certain travel-ban countries. If this may apply to you, contact ISSS before applying or traveling.

To apply for Academic Training (AT) through Drexel, a J-1 student must meet all of these requirements:

- Your DS-2019 was issued by Drexel, not an outside agency (such as Fulbright).
- You are primarily in the U.S. to study, rather than to do academic training.
- You are in good academic standing.
- The training is directly related to the major field of study listed on your DS-2019.
- Your AT is approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date.
- The AT starts no later than 30 days after your program ends.

**Time limits that affect eligibility:**
- Bachelor's and master's students: up to 18 months, or the length of the degree program if shorter (STEM degree students may qualify for a special extension).
- PhD students: up to 36 months, or the length of the program if shorter.
- Non-degree students: the DS-2019 can't extend beyond 24 months in total, including degree time and AT.

**Timing:** Submit your request to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends allowing at least three weeks for processing.

**Upcoming rule change:** A DHS final rule eliminating duration of status was scheduled to take effect September 15, 2026. A September 14, 2026 announcement says a US District Court postponed its effective date, so please check that [announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status) for the current status. The earlier 2025 proposal said post-graduation AT could require a USCIS extension, but that was a proposal, so confirm with an ISSS advisor how this applies to you.

Sources: [Academic Training for J-1 Students](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment), [2025 DHS proposal announcement](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2025/September/DHS-Proposes-to-Replace-Duration-of-Status-for-F-and-J-Visa-Holders-with-Fixed-Periods-of-Stay)

Tôi được phép thất nghiệp bao nhiêu ngày? | Tôi đang làm OPT sau khi tốt nghiệp.
records.answer:
Trong thời gian Post-Completion OPT (12 tháng đầu), bạn được phép thất nghiệp tối đa **90 ngày** (tổng cộng). Nếu bạn được duyệt gia hạn STEM OPT 24 tháng, bạn có thêm **60 ngày**, nên tổng tối đa là **150 ngày**.

**Cách tính:**
- Mỗi ngày (kể cả cuối tuần) không có việc làm hợp lệ, tính từ ngày bắt đầu OPT trên thẻ EAD, được tính là một ngày thất nghiệp.
- Làm việc từ xa được phép, nhưng với Post-Completion OPT phải làm ít nhất 20 giờ mỗi tuần.

**Lưu ý:**
- Bạn phải báo cho ISSS nếu bị gián đoạn hoặc mất việc.
- Trong STEM OPT, nếu mất việc hoặc nghỉ việc trước khi kết thúc, bạn phải báo ISSS và nộp bản đánh giá cuối cùng trên Form I-983 trong vòng 10 ngày.
- Nếu sắp hết giới hạn thất nghiệp, bạn phải hành động **trước** ngày thất nghiệp cuối cùng, ví dụ chuyển sang trường SEVP khác, đổi bậc học, rời khỏi Hoa Kỳ, hoặc có biện pháp khác để duy trì tình trạng. Nếu không, bạn sẽ vi phạm tình trạng F-1.

Nếu bạn lo ngại về số ngày thất nghiệp của mình, hãy liên hệ cố vấn ISSS để được xác nhận.
